USED CAR LOT AGING PLANNER · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER

Which aged units should you wholesale today, and when should the rest go?

"Wait until it sells" quietly pays floorplan interest, curtailments and lot costs on units that are worth less every week. Paste your inventory — days on lot, total cost, floored amount, expected retail and wholesale values and how fast each falls — and get each unit's true carrying cost to date and per day, the exact best day to wholesale it under your own numbers, which units to wholesale now, ranked by what they earn per $1,000 of floorplan line per day, and the dollars a wait-until-it-sells policy leaves behind.

For independent used-car dealers with 1 to 60 units on a floorplan line. Nothing is uploaded: the text box is analysed in this browser and never leaves your device.

    Prefer a CLI?

    Same logic, zero dependencies, one command — reads a file or stdin:

    node cli.mjs plan lot.csv --apr 9 --cash-rate 6 --max-age 180 --curtail 90:10,120:10,150:10
cat lot.csv | node cli.mjs plan - --line-value 2 --json

    Get cli.mjs and engine.mjs — Node 18+, nothing to install, no network call. More: When should a used car dealer wholesale an aged unit? Floorplan and price-drop math.

    What's recognised

    InputHandling

    The wholesale day is exact for the numbers you type. Prices fall in a straight line at the rates you give, and the chance of a retail sale is the same every day; seasonality, a price cut that speeds a sale up, reconditioning still to do, trade-in and F&I income, and your lender's own fees and audit rules are not modelled. The ranking is a way to see where line earns least, not an instruction.

    Common questions

    Does it upload my inventory?

    No. The browser page works on the text you paste, in your own browser, and never sends it anywhere. The CLI reads a local file or stdin and makes no network call.

    How is the wholesale day found?

    While a unit is unsold the only thing that changes is its age, so every plan is 'retail until day T, then wholesale'. The tool works backwards from your floorplan limit one day at a time and finds the best T exactly for the numbers you give; the tests compare it with computing every T directly.

    What is the true carrying cost of a unit?

    Floorplan interest on the balance still owed, what your own cash in the unit (equity plus curtailments paid) could earn elsewhere, and the daily holding cost you enter for insurance, lot space and upkeep, added up day by day from the day it arrived.

    Why rank by dollars per $1,000 of line per day?

    A floorplan line is the scarce thing on a small lot. A unit that adds $600 over wholesale but ties up $16,000 of line for four months earns less per dollar of line than a fresh unit would. The ranking shows where line is earning the least, so you know which units to move first when you need room to buy.

    Who is it for?

    Independent used-car dealers with roughly 1 to 60 units on a floorplan line, deciding which aged units to keep retailing and which to send to auction or a wholesaler.

when-should-a-used-car-dealer-wholesale-.text:
Used Car Lot Aging Planner · guide

When should a used car dealer wholesale an aged unit? Floorplan and price-drop math

Short answer: keep a unit listed only while one more day is worth more than it costs — the chance it retails that day times the gap over wholesale, against the day's floorplan interest, the cost of your own cash in it, the lot and insurance, and the wholesale value it loses by sitting. Once that stops being true for good, the auction check today beats the one next month.

A worked lot

Ten units from 6 to 140 days old, floorplan at 9% with curtailments of 10% at 90, 120 and 150 days and payoff at 180, your own cash worth 6% a year, and $6 to $12 a day of insurance, lot and upkeep per unit.

  • The lot costs $118.80 a day to carry and has already spent $6,877.07. The 140-day Fusion alone has carried $1,412.27.
  • Three units — the Altima, the Malibu and the Fusion — are worth more wholesaled today, freeing $17,130.00 of floorplan line.
  • Two more get a date: the Wrangler at day 115 and the Tahoe at day 147 if they have not retailed by then. The other five retail to the limit.
  • Holding every unit until it retails or hits 180 days is worth $1,117.35 less in expected dollars, and uses 4,164 thousand-dollar-days of line against 2,934.

If freed line would earn $2 per $1,000 a day on a fresh unit, the answer moves: five units go now, freeing $44,380.00, and waiting costs $4,885.68 counting that line value.

What to feed it

  1. Total cost: purchase, buy fee, transport and reconditioning — everything in the car.
  2. Floored amount: what the lender advanced. The rest, and each curtailment you pay, is your own cash.
  3. Expected retail price and how many dollars it falls every 30 days, from your comps and your markdown habit.
  4. Wholesale value today after auction fees, and how fast it falls.
  5. Expected days to retail at that price — one over this is the daily chance of a sale.

Check your floorplan agreement first: curtailment dates, payoff terms and audit rules are your lender's, and they override any plan.

Questions

When should a used car dealer wholesale an aged unit?

When the expected gain from one more day on the lot (the chance it retails times the gap between retail and wholesale) no longer covers that day's carrying cost plus how much the wholesale value falls in a day, and will not again before the floorplan limit. The planner finds that day exactly from your own numbers.

What does it cost to carry a used car on floorplan?

Interest on the balance still owed, what your own cash in the car (equity plus curtailments paid) could earn elsewhere, and insurance, lot and upkeep. On the worked lot that is $118.80 a day across ten units, and $6,877.07 already spent.

Is waiting until it sells a good policy?

Not for every unit. On the worked lot it is worth $1,117.35 less in expected dollars than wholesaling three units now and setting a wholesale day for two more, and it uses about 42% more floorplan line.

It is not financial, tax, legal, lending or business advice, and you are responsible for verifying its output, for the numbers you enter, and for your floorplan agreement. The worked example is illustrative arithmetic, not a forecast of what any vehicle will sell for.
